sources.entry: Konverter - Menu bar file converter and image compressor operated by dragging files onto a radial wheel. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/davidpraznik/Konverter) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: A macOS menu bar app that converts files and compresses images by dragging them onto a radial wheel, with a separate wheel for preparing images for the web.
summary.what_it_does: Konverter lives in the macOS menu bar and reacts to file drags from Finder. Holding Shift while dragging opens a conversion wheel; dropping a file on a segment converts it and saves the result next to the original. Images can be converted to PNG, WEBP, JPG, AVIF, HEIC, PDF, TIFF or BMP, and video to MP4, GIF or M4A (audio only). Holding Command opens an image tools wheel with "For web" (resize to a chosen longest side, compress, convert to sRGB, remove metadata) and "Strip metadata" (removes EXIF and location data without other changes). Several files can be dropped at once, and name clashes get a number appended. Settings cover launch at login, update checks, the tools key, the wheel style (Glass or Solid), and For web defaults. The README says it only listens for mouse presses and does work during drags and conversions, with an optional daily update check.
use_cases: convert images between formats by dragging files
compress images for publishing on the web
strip EXIF and location metadata from photos
convert video to GIF or MP4 quickly
extract audio from video as M4A
batch convert several files from Finder
how_to_run: Clone the repository and open Konverter.xcodeproj in Xcode.
Xcode resolves the libwebp Swift package on first open.
Select the Release scheme and run the app.
Start Konverter; it lives in the menu bar.
Drag files from Finder while holding Shift (conversion wheel) or Command (image tools wheel).
For downloaded builds, open via System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway, since they are not notarized.
notable: Energy-efficient design: drag detection runs only while the mouse button is held, with no background work apart from an optional daily update check
Radial wheel UI opened at the cursor, with Shift for conversion and Command for image tools
One-step For web preset: resize, compress, sRGB conversion and metadata removal, with lossless PNG
Configurable tools key (Shift+Command) to avoid accidental triggers when switching apps with Command+Tab
caveats: Requires macOS 14.6 or later; the README says it was tested only on macOS 27
Builds from GitHub are not notarized, so macOS blocks first launch and needs a manual approval step
